# demo_accel registers

<!-- Generated by hwsw/regmap.py (regmap/1) from regmap demo_accel 0.1.0; model sha256 e5832198fae5fdbdd3437b65db3f2cb5aa338b51c2a6cd2a28571e5eb2a538c7.  Do not edit: change the YAML and run python3 -m hwsw.regmap gen. -->

Control and status of a stream accelerator with a descriptor ring and one interrupt. This block differs from the house register conventions (docs/hwsw.md) in 5 ways: unmapped addresses inside the block: SLVERR and read 0 (house: a read answers SLVERR with data 0 and a write answers OKAY and changes nothing); the error capture has an interrupt (house: none); a write whose strobes cover part of a multi-byte field answers SLVERR and changes nothing (house: accepted, only the strobed bytes change); an access whose address bits [1:0] are not 0 answers SLVERR (house: the low bits are not decoded); a write of 1 to a reserved bit answers SLVERR and changes nothing (house: ignored).

Interface profile: `strict` (for bring-up, safety or verification-heavy work: every access the block cannot take as asked answers SLVERR (a hole, an unaligned address, a partial write to a multi-byte field, a write of 1 to a reserved bit), the error-capture registers are on with their interrupt, and a value wider than the bus must be a snapshot group). No setting differs from the profile.

Settings: `unmapped=slverr error_capture=on+irq partial_write=slverr unaligned=slverr reserved_write=slverr wide_values=snapshot`.

AXI4-Lite, 32-bit registers, a 0x1000-byte window (address bits [11:2] decoded). Unmapped addresses: SLVERR and read 0. Version 0.1.0; model sha256 `e5832198fae5fdbd`.

| 0xffc | ERR_STATUS | 0x00000000 | Error-capture flags and count. |

Reset is what a read returns after reset with every hardware input low.

## Access types

| Access | Meaning |
|---|---|
| RW | read/write: software writes the value; hardware sees it on an output |
| RO | read-only: the value comes from a hardware input (or is a constant); writes are ignored |
| W1C | write 1 to clear: hardware sets bits with a pulse input; software clears a bit by writing 1 to it; a set and a clear in the same clock leave the bit set (no event is lost) |
| W1S | write 1 to set: software sets bits by writing 1 (a doorbell); hardware clears them with a pulse input; a set and a clear in the same clock leave the bit set |
| W1P | write 1 to pulse: each bit written as 1 gives a one-clock pulse on an output; reads return 0 |
| RO const | read-only constant, fixed when the block is built |

## Behaviour

- **Interface profile.** `strict` (for bring-up, safety or verification-heavy work: every access the block cannot take as asked answers SLVERR (a hole, an unaligned address, a partial write to a multi-byte field, a write of 1 to a reserved bit), the error-capture registers are on with their interrupt, and a value wider than the bus must be a snapshot group). No setting differs from the profile. The profile is chosen once per design (spec.yaml `interfaces:`) and may be overridden per block and per setting; the settings it bundles are listed in docs/hwsw.md.
- **Unmapped addresses.** An address inside this block's 0x1000-byte window that holds no register answers SLVERR and reads 0, for a read and for a write (a write there is ignored). A SLVERR on a load is expected to be a synchronous external abort on an Arm CPU, so a stray access stops the program; a SLVERR on a posted write is expected to arrive late and imprecisely. What an Arm CPU does with these responses is expected, not yet measured on this project's platforms (docs/hwsw.md). Addresses outside the window belong to the interconnect (an AXI crossbar answers DECERR there).
- **Error capture.** Every access to an unmapped address is recorded, whatever the response above. An access this profile answers with SLVERR (an unaligned address, a rejected write: see Partial writes, Access width and alignment, Reserved bits) is recorded in the same way, so the registers do not say which cause it was. ERR_STATUS.STICKY (0xffc) is set by the first one since the last clear; ERR_ADDR (0xff8) then holds its word-aligned address inside the window (the address bits the block decodes) and ERR_STATUS.IS_WRITE says whether it was a write. Later bad accesses do not replace them: ERR_STATUS.COUNT counts every one, saturating at 255. Write 1 to STICKY to clear the record (STICKY and COUNT go to 0; ERR_ADDR and IS_WRITE keep their last values and are meaningful only while STICKY is 1). A bad access in the same clock as that clear is not lost: it starts the new record (STICKY 1, COUNT 1). A bad read and a bad write in the same clock count 2 and the read is the one recorded. Reads of the capture registers have no side effects. ERR_STATUS.IRQ_EN (reset 0) enables the interrupt: `irq_o` is high while STICKY is 1 and IRQ_EN is 1 (registered, one clock after the cause).
- **Reserved bits.** Bits that belong to no field read 0. A write that has 1 in a reserved bit (in a byte lane whose strobe is 1) answers SLVERR and changes nothing at all, not even the other fields of the register: write reserved bits as 0, or write back only what you read (reserved bits read 0). A 0 in a reserved bit is accepted.
- **Reads have no side effects.** Reading any register changes nothing, so a debugger or a retried read is safe. A read-modify-write must write the W1C, W1S and W1P bits as 0 (here CTRL.OVERFLOW, IRQ_STATUS.DONE, IRQ_STATUS.ERROR, ERR_STATUS.STICKY, DOORBELL.QUEUE, CMD.START, CMD.FLUSH, CMD.SNAP), or it clears, sets or pulses them: write back only the RW bits of what was read. To start, pop or acknowledge something, write 1 to its W1P bit: CMD.START, CMD.FLUSH. A snapshot is taken by writing 1 to its trigger: CMD.SNAP. Doorbells are W1S bits: DOORBELL.QUEUE. A write to a read-only register is answered OKAY and ignored, unless it puts a 1 in a reserved bit of that register (see Reserved bits).
- **Same-clock priority (the house convention).** W1C bits (CTRL.OVERFLOW, IRQ_STATUS.DONE, IRQ_STATUS.ERROR, ERR_STATUS.STICKY): a hardware set in the same clock as a software clear wins, so the bit stays set and no event is lost. W1S bits (DOORBELL.QUEUE): a software set in the same clock as a hardware clear wins, so the set is not lost.
- **Partial writes.** Byte strobes (WSTRB) are honoured: a byte whose strobe is 0 keeps its value, and in it W1C, W1S and W1P bits count as 0 (nothing is cleared, set or pulsed). A write whose strobes cover only part of a writable field that spans several byte lanes answers SLVERR and changes nothing (the whole write is rejected), because the field would be written torn; such fields: CTRL.SCALE, RING_BASE.ADDR, SCRATCH.VALUE. A write that covers every lane of such a field, or none of its lanes, is accepted, and so is any strobe pattern on a field inside one byte lane. A write with all strobes 0 changes nothing and answers OKAY.
- **Access width and alignment.** 32-bit registers on a 32-bit AXI4-Lite bus. AXI4-Lite has no transfer size: a CPU's byte or halfword load reads the whole word, and its store arrives as a word write with fewer strobes (see Partial writes). An address whose bits [1:0] are not 0 answers SLVERR: a read returns 0 and a write changes nothing, whatever it would address, even an unmapped word; only bits [11:2] are decoded, so the window repeats every 0x1000 bytes. Use aligned 32-bit accesses.
- **Values wider than 32 bits.** Snapshot group JOB_CYCLES (64 bits: JOB_CYCLES_LO.VALUE, then JOB_CYCLES_HI.VALUE, low part first): write 1 to CMD.SNAP to copy the whole value into shadow registers in one clock (the hardware's values as they are in the clock the write takes effect; see Clock domain and timing), then read the parts in any order; they belong to the same instant. A read without a new snapshot returns the copy from the last one (stale), not the live value; the copies read 0 after reset. Every other register is read on its own, so a value split across two of them can tear. This profile requires a snapshot group for a hardware value wider than the bus; the generator recognises the register pairs NAME_LO/NAME_HI, _LOW/_HIGH, _LSW/_MSW and _L/_H, so name the halves that way or put the value in a group yourself.
- **Reset.** `aresetn`, synchronous, active low (sampled on the rising edge of `aclk`). Every stored field takes the reset value in its table; W1P bits read 0; snapshot copies read 0. Not reset by this block: the RO fields that read a hardware input (STATUS.BUSY, STATUS.LEVEL, RING_HEAD.INDEX); they show their input's value.
- **Interrupt.** `irq_o` is a level output from a register: high while any bit of IRQ_STATUS (DONE, ERROR) is set together with the same bit of IRQ_ENABLE. Clear the cause by writing 1 to its IRQ_STATUS bit (W1C); the line falls one clock after the clear takes effect. A clear never loses a new event (a hardware set in the same clock wins), but events of the same cause between the handler's read and its clear merge into one: count them elsewhere if each one matters. Clear the cause before unmasking the line at the interrupt controller.
- **Clock domain and timing.** Every field is in the `aclk` domain; hardware inputs must be synchronous to `aclk` (the block has no synchronisers). A write takes effect on the hardware in the clock its write response (BVALID) is raised, and a W1P pulse is high for exactly that clock. A read returns the hardware's values as they were in the clock the read address was accepted.

## ID (0x000)

Block identity; software checks it before touching anything else.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31:16 | MAGIC | RO const | 0x64a0 | fixed pattern 0x64A0 |
| 15:0 | VERSION | RO const | 0x100 | register-map version 1.0 |

## CTRL (0x004)

Configuration; written while the block is idle.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 27:16 | SCALE | RW | 0x100 | output gain, unsigned 4.8 fixed point |
| 8 | OVERFLOW | W1C | 0x0 | an input beat arrived while the block was disabled |
| 6:4 | MODE | RW | 0x2 | kernel select |
| 0 | ENABLE | RW | 0x0 | 1 lets the block accept stream data |

## CMD (0x008)

Commands; reading returns 0.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | SNAP | W1P | 0 | copy JOB_CYCLES (both halves) into its shadow registers |
| 1 | FLUSH | W1P | 0 | drop buffered data |
| 0 | START | W1P | 0 | start one job |

| 0 | BUSY | RO | hw | a job is running |

## ERR_ADDR (0xff8)

Address of the first unmapped access since the last clear.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11:0 | ADDR | RO | 0x0 | word-aligned address, inside the window, of the first unmapped access since the last clear; valid while STICKY is 1 |

## ERR_STATUS (0xffc)

Error-capture flags and count.

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15:8 | COUNT | RO | 0x0 | unmapped accesses since the last clear, saturating at 255 |
| 2 | IRQ_EN | RW | 0x0 | 1 raises irq_o while STICKY is 1 |
| 1 | IS_WRITE | RO | 0x0 | the recorded access was a write; valid while STICKY is 1 |
| 0 | STICKY | W1C | 0x0 | an unmapped access happened since the last clear; write 1 to clear (also clears COUNT) |

## Snapshot groups

| Group | Trigger | Fields, low part first | Bits | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JOB_CYCLES | CMD.SNAP | JOB_CYCLES_LO.VALUE, JOB_CYCLES_HI.VALUE | 64 | a 64-bit counter read as two registers; take a snapshot first so the halves agree |
